reason: The hypothesis relies on precipitation strengthening in a BCC refractory HEA, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) describes different alloy systems (NbMoTaWVTi with TiO particles and Al0.7CoCrFeNi with L12 precipitates in an fcc/B2 matrix) and does not provide specific prior data on Hf-rich precipitate formation, thermal stability, or strengthening in TiVNbTa. The key premises about Hf-induced precipitation and its effects are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Hf addition to TiVNbTa can form fine, thermally stable precipitates within the BCC matrix
These precipitates will impede dislocation motion and raise high-temperature yield strength
The continuous BCC matrix will preserve ductility comparable to the baseline
A homogenization treatment at ~1273 K will produce a uniform nanoscale precipitate distribution without brittle intermetallics
The strengthening mechanism is analogous to precipitation strengthening observed in other HEAs
